key_insight: For a synthetic epidemiological model, embedded closure learning achieves the best average accuracy, while staged learning trades moderately higher error for substantially fewer model evaluations and more robust optimization.
engineering_relevance: Staged closure learning can reduce training costs when repeated simulator calls are expensive and qualitative predictive behavior is sufficient.
method: Compare embedded and staged data-driven closure learning in a synthetic susceptible–infected–quarantined–recovered (SIQR) model.
Use data assimilation to infer state and closure trajectories from observations.
Train the staged machine-learning closure offline on assimilated trajectories rather than repeatedly invoking the simulator.
evidence_signal: Evaluation on an SIQR model with a nonlinear, state-dependent quarantine closure shows comparable qualitative behavior for staged learning, but moderately greater error than embedded training.
watch_item: The reported trade-off is demonstrated on one synthetic model and may not generalize to other dynamical systems.
paper_title: Efficient Closure Learning in Dynamical Systems: A Comparison of Data-Assimilated and Embedded Approaches
